facts.note: The whole map is sixty-four blocks east to west, which is as far as a party should have to walk without arriving somewhere.
Sixty-four blocks north to south as well: the site is square, so no approach is the long way round.
The hall is twelve blocks wide — wide enough that the stair up to the loft costs a third of it and is felt.
The loft stands five blocks over the hall floor, which is the whole of the height a body can fall from by design.
The hall stands eight blocks to its ceiling, which is what makes the loft read as a level above rather than a shelf.
The landing is four blocks to its ceiling: low enough that a body arriving reads it as a threshold and not as a room.
